title: Whole Life Insurance Plan Specifications: Premium Period, Issue Limits and Benefit Basis by Tier
content:
Whole Life Insurance is issued by Ashgrove in six tiers. Each tier is defined by how long premiums are payable, the ages and face amounts at which it is issued, its underwriting basis, whether a graded death benefit applies in the early policy years, whether it shares in dividends, and whether it is a modified endowment contract from issue. Every tier endows at attained age **121**.

## Premium-paying period and maturity

| Tier | How the premium-paying period is measured | Premiums stop at | Maturity (endowment) age |
|---|---|---|---|
| Ashgrove Final Expense Whole Life | To an attained age | Attained age 100 | 121 |
| Ashgrove Whole Life Paid-Up at 100 | To an attained age | Attained age 100 | 121 |
| Ashgrove Whole Life Paid-Up at 65 | To an attained age | Attained age 65 | 121 |
| Ashgrove 20-Pay Whole Life | By policy years | 20 policy years | 121 |
| Ashgrove 10-Pay Whole Life | By policy years | 10 policy years | 121 |
| Ashgrove Single Premium Whole Life | Single premium | 1 premium, paid once | 121 |

## Issue limits and underwriting

Issue ages are ages last birthday. Face amounts are the base face of one policy, in US dollars.

| Tier | Issue ages | Smallest base face | Largest base face | Underwriting basis |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ashgrove Final Expense Whole Life | 50 to 85 | 5000 | 40000 | Simplified issue |
| Ashgrove Whole Life Paid-Up at 100 | 0 to 85 | 25000 | 10000000 | Full medical |
| Ashgrove Whole Life Paid-Up at 65 | 0 to 55 | 25000 | 10000000 | Full medical |
| Ashgrove 20-Pay Whole Life | 0 to 75 | 25000 | 10000000 | Full medical |
| Ashgrove 10-Pay Whole Life | 0 to 75 | 25000 | 10000000 | Full medical |
| Ashgrove Single Premium Whole Life | 0 to 85 | 10000 | 2000000 | Full medical |

Entry to the Ashgrove Final Expense Whole Life does not turn on every health question being answered no for a level benefit. The Ashgrove Single Premium Whole Life is entered with the single premium paid at application.

## Benefit basis, dividends and tax status

| Tier | Graded benefit period (policy years from issue) | Graded benefit, as a multiple of premiums paid | Participating (eligible for annual dividends) | Modified endowment contract from issue |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Ashgrove Final Expense Whole Life | 2 | 1.1 | No | No |
| Ashgrove Whole Life Paid-Up at 100 | 0 (level benefit from issue) | 0 | Yes | No |
| Ashgrove Whole Life Paid-Up at 65 | 0 (level benefit from issue) | 0 | Yes | No |
| Ashgrove 20-Pay Whole Life | 0 (level benefit from issue) | 0 | Yes | No |
| Ashgrove 10-Pay Whole Life | 0 (level benefit from issue) | 0 | Yes | No |
| Ashgrove Single Premium Whole Life | 0 (level benefit from issue) | 0 | Yes | Yes |

A graded benefit period of 0 means the tier pays a level benefit from issue, and a graded multiple of 0 accompanies it.

## Reading the schedule

- **Attained-age tiers versus policy-year tiers.** Premiums on the Paid-Up at 100 and Paid-Up at 65 tiers, and on the Final Expense tier, stop by reference to the insured's attained age (100 or 65); on the 20-Pay and 10-Pay tiers they stop after a fixed number of policy years (20 or 10), whatever the insured's age.
- **Example (hypothetical applicant aged 60).** Age 60 lies inside the issue ages of the Final Expense tier (50 to 85), the Paid-Up at 100 tier (0 to 85), the 20-Pay and 10-Pay tiers (0 to 75) and the Single Premium tier (0 to 85), and outside the Paid-Up at 65 tier, whose highest issue age is 55.
- **Example (hypothetical face of 45000 dollars).** It is above the largest Final Expense face (40000) and inside the face limits of every other tier.
